Folks — forwarding Sara's ask. Quick summary from my side (I gathered this from the rollout notes and infra runbook):

- What happened: EdgeRelay was brought in as a temporary ingest relay during a phased rollout (2026-05-03 through 2026-05-10) to capture debug telemetry for a subset of customers impacted by a config migration.
- Data types: only telemetry/ingest-level request metadata and anonymized traces; we did NOT route customer content or model input/output to EdgeRelay. No PII or prompt content.
- Retention: default retention on EdgeRelay was 7 days. We created one compliance snapshot (derived metrics only) and exported it to an internal S3 bucket before decommissioning.
- Hosting: EdgeRelay nodes were in us-west-2 (no cross-border transfers).
- Keys/access: no external KMS/HSM access. The process used our internal CMK (redwood-prod-kms) and access was restricted to the infra service account.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you produce the signed addendum and the attestation note Redmond Legal used (if available)? Please attach the exact addendum file and the minimal attestation text.
- Jonas: please confirm the S3 export path + string that we can hand over as evidence (and whether logs were redacted).
- I'll assemble the package and reply to Sara by EOD.

If anything above is inaccurate, flag it here.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara — thanks for the patience. Attached is a short evidence package addressing your checklist. Summary below and files attached:

Summary (short):
- Subprocessor: EdgeRelay (temporary relay) — active 2026-05-03 -> 2026-05-10.

- Keys/access: no external KMS/HSM; used internal CMK redwood-prod-kms. EdgeRelay had no admin access to customer-managed keys.
